lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes, FPGA
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: May 2021 to April 2022 is a 10-month period with no study or work listed.
items.because: Readers may ask what you were doing during the gap.

items.says: Education appears before Experience.
“Update speed by 60%” does not identify what was measured.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether it refers to download time, end-to-end update time, or another measure.

items.says: The test-rig bullet gives the test volume but not what the tests achieved.
items.because: The scale is clear, but the value of the testing is not.

items.says: “That ran” adds an unnecessary relative clause.
“Which found the root cause” makes the logger’s result indirect and wordy.
Sampling a 5 kHz signal at 8 kHz cannot capture it without aliasing.
items.because: An 8 kHz sampling rate has a Nyquist frequency of 4 kHz, so the 5 kHz component will alias.

items.says: The bullet describes an unvalidated capability rather than an observed detection result.
Declaring a shared counter volatile does not fix a race condition.
items.because: Volatile affects compiler access optimization but does not ensure atomic access or coordinate the interrupt handler and main loop.

items.says: “Fixed a race condition” does not state the observable effect of the fix.
items.because: Readers cannot see what failure or user-visible problem the fix eliminated.

items.says: The jitter change from 120 to 15 microseconds is an 87.5% reduction, not a 60% reduction.
items.because: The decrease is 105 microseconds, or 87.5% of the original 120 microseconds.

items.says: “Rewrote the motor-controller firmware” names the scope but not the technical change.
The jitter and fault reductions are buried after the fleet scope.
“Automated end-of-line tests” does not say how the tests were automated.
“The findings updated the reflow profile” makes the findings, rather than a person or team, the actor.
The calibration-procedure bullet gives no technical detail about the procedure.
“IoT solution” does not say what you built or how it works.
items.because: Readers cannot assess your contribution without a concrete design or implementation detail.

items.says: “Redefines sustainable environmental sensing” gives no specific result or evidence.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what changed or why the claim is credible.

items.says: The strongest project result is not the opening bullet.
“Openly” adds no useful information to the publication claim.
“Worked on firmware and testing” gives neither a result nor the specific work you performed.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what changed or what technical skill the work required.

items.says: The dashboard-firmware bullet does not say what the firmware did or what the testing established.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what function it enabled, what behavior was checked, or why the work mattered.

items.says: “Was written and tested” is passive and hides who performed the work.
The dashboard-firmware bullet is not the opening bullet, although it is the strongest line.
The robot-fleet rewrite and its results are attributed to both this project and the later Voltline role.
items.because: The matching claims appear to describe the same achievement, but the dates place them in different periods.

items.says: “Rewrote motor-control firmware” is broad.
items.because: Readers cannot tell which firmware change produced the results.

items.says: The improvement figures have no stated comparison point.
items.because: “Eightfold” and “more than half” do not identify the baseline used.

items.says: The bullets do not present one clear Formula Student contribution.
items.because: The dashboard firmware and robot-fleet claims concern different systems, making it hard to tell what belongs to the project.
